reader.requirement: At --std 85 a START naming an indexed file in random access mode must be refused (with or without the KEY phrase); START on sequential (explicit or default) or dynamic access is legal.

edition-consulted.switches: Year < 2002: mandatory INVALID KEY (SR3); does not decide SR1

reader.edition-search: the SR1 test (file.AccessMode == Random -> COBOL0862) reads no edition; grep DialectLevel|Edition.Year in KeyedIoBinder.cs (no hits); FIRST/LAST gates live in VersionConformancePass and are not on this path
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb325-start-random-access covers the random refusal; the accepted sequential/dynamic/default forms are not exercised

probes.printed: error COBOL0862: START on 'IXF': the access mode shall be sequential or dynamic

probes.expected: accepted; no ACCESS clause means sequential; KEY NOT < positions at BBBB

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.7.3 SR1  (║4.7.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: There is one edition-agnostic test on access mode, made before any phrase is examined. The accepted forms position correctly at run time.

refuter.evidence: --std 85. r5_global_rnd.cob: a nested program STARTs a GLOBAL indexed file declared ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM in the outer program and gets 'COBOL0862: START on 'IXF': the access mode shall be sequential or dynamic'. KeyedIoBinder.cs#BindStart line 319 tests file.AccessMode == Random, with no edition read. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.7.3 SR1  (4.7.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1'.
